label: Finite past as first time versus bounded metric age
term: finite past as first time versus bounded metric age
resolution: The existing PastIsFinite predicate means an earlier-free time at or before now; PastIsInfinite means each time through now has an earlier time. Neither denotes unbounded metric duration or finite event cardinality. This control uses the original predicates on (0,1] and a chosen Real clock to show no first moment can coexist with bounded age. The absence of a first moment does not prove unbounded age in this profile; conversely, bounded age alone does not supply an earliest time. Time points here are mathematical indices, not alternative complete histories or causal-support vertices. No physical realization or finite-resource hypothesis follows.
